chapterTitle: Advanced Option Strategies: Principal-Protected Notes, Spreads, Combinations, and Arbitrage

beatOutlines.textOutline: A retail investor asks how to invest in the stock market without risking capital; a mentor introduces Principal-Protected Notes (PPNs) ([fact-01]).

beatOutlines.textOutline: The mentor explains the dual structure: zero-coupon government bonds guarantee 100% principal preservation at maturity ([fact-01]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remaining capital is allocated to call options on an index, providing upside market participation with zero downside risk ([fact-01]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Vertical Spreads Matrix: Bull vs. Bear Call and Put Spreads

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Bull Spreads: Bull Call Spread (net debit, BE = K_1 + Debit, Max Profit = (K_2 - K_1) - Debit) and Bull Put Spread (net credit, BE = K_2 - Credit, Max Loss = (K_2 - K_1) - Credit) ([fact-04], [fact-05]).

scenes.title: Box Spread Present Value Arbitrage Valuation

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine Box Spread structure combining a bull call spread and bear put spread across strikes K_1 < K_2, guaranteeing a constant terminal payoff of K_2 - K_1 ([fact-08]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare market box price against the no-arbitrage present value rule Box Price = (K_2 - K_1) * e^(-r*T), identifying arbitrage opportunities when initial debit falls below present value ([fact-08]).

summarySteps: 1. Principal-Protected Notes ([fact-01]): Combine zero-coupon government bonds for 100% principal preservation with call options for upside market participation.
2. Covered Calls ([fact-02], [fact-11]): Combine long stock with a short call, establishing downside break-even at S_0 - c and capping maximum profit at (K - S_0) + c.
3. Protective Puts ([fact-03]): Combine long stock with a long put to establish break-even at S_0 + p and cap maximum loss at (S_0 - K) + p.
4. Bull Call Spreads ([fact-04], [fact-10]): Buy lower strike K_1 and sell higher strike K_2 as a net debit to capture limited upside profit with defined max loss.
5. Bull Put Spreads ([fact-05]): Buy lower strike put K_1 and sell higher strike put K_2 as a net credit transaction to generate immediate income.
6. Bear Spreads ([fact-06], [fact-07]): Utilize bear put debit spreads or bear call credit spreads to profit from downward stock price movements.
7. Box Spreads ([fact-08]): Combine bull call and bear put spreads to lock in guaranteed terminal payoff K_2 - K_1, enforcing present value pricing via Box Price = (K_2 - K_1) * e^(-r*T).
8. Butterfly Spreads ([fact-09]): Combine two long calls at outer strikes K_1, K_3 and two short calls at middle strike K_2 (where K_2 = (K_1 + K_3)/2) to profit from neutral range-bound volatility.
bottomTakeaway: Advanced option strategies synthesize zero-coupon bonds, hedged stock positions, vertical spreads, and arbitrage boxes to precisely control risk, income, and directional exposure ([fact-01], [fact-02], [fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-08], [fact-09]).
